title: Learn to Read Tarot
introduction: Learn the foundations, then choose a practical tutorial for the reading you want to make.

articles.title: How to Read Tarot
articles.summary: Prepare, draw, and connect the cards in a clear reading.

sections.heading: Choose Your Focus
sections.body: Decide what you want to explore, then choose a reading whose positions fit that focus.

sections.heading: Draw the Cards
sections.body: Shuffle while holding the focus in mind, then draw and place each card in position order.

sections.heading: Build the Reading
sections.body: Read each card in its position, then connect repeated images, contrasts, and changes across the spread.

articles.title: Shuffle and Draw
articles.summary: Prepare the deck and begin a reading one card at a time.

sections.heading: Prepare the Deck
sections.body: Choose the reading first so you know how many cards to draw and what each position means.

sections.heading: Shuffle
sections.body: Keep the focus in mind while you shuffle, then stop when you are ready to begin.

sections.heading: Draw in Order
sections.body: Draw one card for each position from left to right and turn them over in the order you prefer.

articles.title: Symbols and Patterns
articles.summary: Observe the images and find connections between the cards.

sections.heading: Look First
sections.body: Notice figures, objects, colors, numbers, and movement before opening the reference meaning.

sections.heading: Compare the Cards
sections.body: Look for repeated suits, numbers, symbols, moods, directions, or clear contrasts across the spread.

sections.heading: Connect to Position
sections.body: Relate each visible pattern to the role of its position so the spread stays focused.

articles.title: Build Your Interpretation
articles.summary: Join positions, symbols, and meanings into one clear response.

sections.heading: Read Each Position
sections.body: Start with one card at a time and connect its meaning directly to the position it occupies.

sections.heading: Find the Relationship
sections.body: Compare the cards to see what supports, changes, repeats, or challenges the first idea.

sections.heading: Say It Simply
sections.body: Bring the positions together in one or two sentences that return to the original focus.

articles.title: One Card
articles.summary: Use one card for a clear focus.

sections.heading: Choose the Focus
sections.body: Use this reading when one central idea, influence, or point of attention is enough.

sections.heading: Draw One Card
sections.body: Hold the focus in mind, shuffle, draw one card, and turn it face up.

sections.heading: Read the Message
sections.body: Notice the image and keywords, then connect the upright meaning to the focus you chose.

articles.title: Past, Present, Possible Direction
articles.summary: Read how a situation developed and where it may be heading.

sections.heading: The Three Positions
sections.body: Card 1 is the Past, card 2 is the Present, and card 3 is the Possible Direction.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Shuffle and draw three cards from left to right, keeping each card in its assigned position.

sections.heading: Read the Sequence
sections.body: Read each position first, then notice what continues or changes from the first card to the third.

articles.title: Situation, Challenge, Guidance
articles.summary: See the issue, its challenge, and the guidance offered.

sections.heading: The Three Positions
sections.body: Card 1 is the Situation, card 2 is the Challenge, and card 3 is the Guidance.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Hold the issue in mind, then shuffle and draw three cards from left to right.

sections.heading: Connect the Reading
sections.body: Read how the Challenge affects the Situation and how the Guidance responds to both cards.

articles.title: You, Other Person, Connection
articles.summary: Explore two people and the connection between them.

sections.heading: The Three Positions
sections.body: Card 1 represents You, card 2 the Other Person, and card 3 the Connection.

sections.heading: Lay Out the Cards
sections.body: Think of the relationship, then shuffle and draw three cards from left to right.

sections.heading: Read the Dynamic
sections.body: Compare the first two cards and use the third to describe the connection they form together.

articles.title: For, Against, and Destiny
articles.summary: Use three cards to answer one clear yes-or-no question.

sections.heading: Card 1 - For
sections.body: Keep your yes-or-no question in mind, shuffle, and draw the first card. Read it as what favors a yes: the support, strengths, or conditions working for the question.

sections.heading: Card 2 - Against
sections.body: Draw the second card to the right. Read it as what favors a no: the resistance, obstacles, or conditions working against the question.

sections.heading: Card 3 - Destiny
sections.body: Draw the third card to the right. Read it as what Destiny holds, then form the final answer by considering the For and Against cards.

articles.title: Freeform
articles.summary: Use three cards without assigned positions.

sections.heading: Choose the Focus
sections.body: Use Freeform when you want three cards without giving them fixed roles before the draw.

sections.heading: Draw Three Cards
sections.body: Shuffle and draw Card 1, Card 2, and Card 3 from left to right.

sections.heading: Read the Whole
sections.body: Read each card in order, then connect repeated images, contrasts, and movement across all three.
